newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- JUNE 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- JUNE 26.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--Despite initial rejection of the Spraos report on the course to convergence, it appears that the government is slowly coming round to accept the report's recommendations on wage increases for the 1998-1999 period. The one-off charge on company profits to fund unemployment projects is unlikely to get government support however.
--A new public company to be established will play the role of financial adviser and brokerage house to the state, Deputy Finance Minister Nikos Christodoulakis revealed.

--Companies proceeding with investments for modernisation over the past few years have seen an impressive rise in profits and turnover, according to a special survery of 820 firms. The foodstuffs sector continues to remain the leader in industry.

--Prime Minister Costas Simitis has returned to his position for a need for a redistribution of public spending and for employees to undertake part of their pension requirements, and has left open the issue of whether he will implement the Spraos report in full.
--Egnatia Bank was the sole bidder to make an offer for the Bank of Central Greece yesterday, a disappointment for a government expecting offers from the eight banks who had shown interest.

--Low absorption rates for tourism projects included in the Second Community Support Framework are causing problems for both the development ministry and the Greek National Tourist Organisation as there's a risk that funds could be transferred to other sectors.
--Guidelines for state-guaranteed loans to public enterprises and organisations will be tightened up following the news that the state is paying about one trillion drachmas a year for bad loans.
--Commercial and Xiosbank yesterday announced profits for 1996 and said that this year would be even better. Xiosbank psoted profits increased by an impressive 30 percent.
--Efforts to reduce the state's foreign lending are proceeding at satisfactory rates, Christodoulakis said yesterday. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
